D001-D013_h001.question_both:
I’ve been feeling “off” for maybe… eight, nine months now. It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. I still go to the community center to help with the lunch program, but I keep losing track of what I’m doing. I’ll start setting up tables, then suddenly I’m in the storage closet, wondering why I went in there. I misplace the sign‑in sheets, forget who I’ve already spoken to, and my notes are all over the place. It makes simple tasks feel strangely overwhelming.

People tell me I’m always on my feet, fussing with something. I find it hard just to sit quietly, even at home; I’ll get up, straighten things, check the kettle, walk from room to room. At the center, I catch myself chattering on and on, filling silences, even when I know I should let others speak.

I do feel more low and tired than I used to since my husband passed, and my mind wanders a lot—sometimes to worries, sometimes to nothing in particular. I can’t tell if the difficulty focusing is part of feeling down or if it’s just how my brain works now.
D001-D013_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been kind of scattered, honestly, even as a kid. Teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright but “never focused” and “constantly talking.” My parents said I never sat still, always fidgeting or running from one thing to another, and that hasn’t really changed much, even now at 67. When I’m at the community center, I sign up for too many projects at once. I start sorting donations, then get distracted by a conversation, then wander off to reorganize a shelf I suddenly notice is messy. I lose track of what I was doing and it’s hard to keep things in order.

My mind jumps around a lot; I’ll be folding clothes and suddenly I’m lost in some random thought about something from years ago. People tell me I talk too much and interrupt without meaning to. I feel like I’m always “on,” like there’s a motor running inside me.

Since my husband died, I’ve been sad, more tired, and cry more easily, but the trouble focusing and staying organized has been there my whole life, not just since I started feeling low.
D001-D013_h001.question_b:
It’s been about four months now that I just haven’t been myself. Since my husband passed a few years ago I’ve had ups and downs, but these last months it feels like I’ve sunk into a hole I can’t climb out of. I wake up heavy, dreading the day, and I don’t enjoy my volunteer work at the church like I used to. Most days I’m just sad or numb, and it’s hard to see the point of anything.

During this time my mind feels foggy. I can’t concentrate on simple things—sorting donation lists, planning events, even following a TV show. I lose track of what I’m doing and get pulled off by random thoughts about my husband or worries about the future. I never had these focus problems before I started feeling this low.

I used to be very organized with my projects, but lately I can’t keep tasks straight, and it frustrates me. I pace around the house a lot because I’m too agitated to sit and read, and when I’m with others I sometimes ramble on more than I mean to, just to fill the silence and distract myself from how empty I feel.

My work as an interior designer is getting harder to manage. I lose track of where I am in a project, forget measurements I just took, or misplace samples and invoices. Even in conversations with clients, my mind can drift off to something totally unrelated.

At the same time, I don’t really slow down. My husband jokes I’m like a pinball—pacing around the house, starting five chores at once. I talk a lot, even when I’m telling myself to just keep it brief, and I’ll catch myself jumping in before someone’s finished.

Lately I’ve also just felt kind of worn down and flat, like it all takes more effort than it should, but I’m not sure what’s causing what anymore.

Even as a kid, I couldn’t sit still in class, talked nonstop, and got in trouble for daydreaming or staring out the window. That “restless” feeling never really went away. My husband jokes I’m powered by batteries because I’m always pacing, fiddling with things, or jumping up to start something else.

At work, I constantly misplace samples, forget where I saved files, and jump between projects without finishing what I started. I make elaborate to‑do lists and then get overwhelmed and distracted by emails, noises in the office, or even my own random thoughts. I’ll walk into a room and forget why I went there because my mind has already wandered somewhere else.

The low mood and feeling down are more recent, maybe the past year or so, and seem tied to how much I’m screwing things up and disappointing people. But the trouble focusing, staying organized, and sitting still has been there my whole life, whether I feel sad or relatively okay.
D001-D013_h002.question_b:

I can’t organize anything—samples pile up, I miss deadlines, I reread emails three or four times and still can’t focus. That scatterbrained feeling really only began once my mood sank like this.

I sit at my desk and my mind wanders off into these hopeless thoughts—“What’s the point, you’re failing everyone”—and then an hour has gone by. At home my husband says I pace around the house, fidgeting, picking things up and putting them down, but not actually getting anything done. Sometimes, to fill the silence or distract myself from how low I feel, I just ramble on about work details or trivial stuff, and then feel stupid afterward.

Before this episode, I was busy but effective. I never had this kind of concentration problem or this constant cloud of sadness and guilt hanging over everything.
